definition: A visual analogue scale is a psychometric rating scale used to measure a person’s subjective symptoms or experiences. It works by asking the person to mark a position along a continuous line between two fixed end points.

provenance.scope: Source record C121547; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports a psychometric response scale for assessing subjective characteristics or symptoms, but it does not explicitly support the broader claim that it measures subjective ‘experiences.’

The description of how it works by ‘asking the person to mark a position along a continuous line’ is not stated in the packet; the packet only says it relies on a continuum of possible values between two fixed end-points.
The definition claims it measures “subjective symptoms or experiences.” The packet supports “subjective characteristics or symptoms,” but does not mention “experiences.”

The definition says it “works by asking the person to mark a position along a continuous line.” The packet only states it relies on a continuum of possible result values between two fixed end-points; it does not explicitly describe the method as “mark a position” or as a “line.”
